summary: Serve ordinary agents lists immediately from the latest published roster, with explicit host-local min_cut fences for read-after-write

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes. The change affects reads of the in-memory published agents roster.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. min_cut uses the existing host-local ClaimRecord.store_index returned by writes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention, authority or rules-version change; no coordinated member upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: Ordinary st agents ls and st agents tree stop sending fresh=true and return the newest publication. Right after starting or changing an agent, st agents ls can show the earlier roster; right after daemon startup it can say the roster is still being prepared. Use the same-host receipt cut when you need your own write. Existing fresh=true requests, the agents_list_fresh SDK method, failed-attempt and unchanged-card handling, and latency classification are preserved. Additive min_cut uses the same host-local acceptance index returned by a write, waits at most two seconds and returns retryable agent-roster-cut-not-ready unless the final served publication reaches it. min_cut wins over fresh with one timer and is rejected with a continuation cursor. Older daemons ignore min_cut and return their newest publication; callers compare the served index on the minting host, and Rust agents_list_after rejects an unmet cut. Current-work freshness is unchanged.

downtime.detail: No startup migration or expected service interruption. Reads still require an initial usable roster publication.

manual.detail: No operator action or configuration change. Callers opting into min_cut use a same-host write receipt and check the served cut; existing freshness callers retain their behavior.

recovery.detail: No persistent state changes or new rollback restrictions. Older daemons ignore min_cut and return their newest publication; named-cut clients must compare its host-local snapshot index rather than claim read-after-write.
